questions.q: Which sentence defines a time series best?
options: Values of one measure at different times, kept in time order
Any table that has a date column
A table with more rows than columns
why: A table with a date column can be cross-sectional or panel data. Order and one measure are the key.
Table shape does not define it.

questions.q: A retailer has daily sales for 200 products over 3 years. What is this data?
why: Correct. Many things (products) over many moments.
The days are regular and there are many series.

questions.q: A table lists the height of 50 students measured on one day. What is it?
A daily series should have 31 rows for January but has 28. How many days are missing?
questions.why: 31 − 28 = 3 rows are missing. Find them with full_calendar.difference(s.index).

questions.q: You get a log of user clicks with exact times. You must forecast clicks per hour. What is your first step?
options: Count clicks per hour to make a regular series
why: Correct. Aggregate the event log to a fixed frequency.

questions.q: A colleague splits a daily series 80/20 at random rows, then reports a great test score. What is wrong?
options: Training rows come from after some test rows, so the model sees the future
The test set is too small
why: Correct. Neighbors are related, so a random split leaks information. Split by time.
Random splits are right only when rows are independent.
The size is fine. The method is wrong.

questions.q: pd.infer_freq returns None for your index. What does this tell you?
options: There is no single regular step (gaps or irregular times)
The series has too many rows
why: Correct. Check for missing dates or unequal steps.
An empty index also gives None, but gaps are the usual reason.
